transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-05
Start: 14:30 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Sarah Martinez (CTO, NovaMed), Ethan Park (Head of Security), Renee Liu (Infra)

Summary:
Quick security posture discovery to understand NovaMed's requirements for a production LLM deployment. Main topics: SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data retention, and hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs.

Topics:
- Compliance posture (SOC2/ISO/hipaa)
- Identity and access (SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC)
- Observability & audit logs retention
- Encryption / KMS and key ownership for private deployments
- Data residency and retention policies
- Next steps and benchmarking

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll do a quick intros then jump into your security posture needs. 
[00:10] Sarah Martinez: hi yes thanks, i'm sarah, cto at novamed, we've got ethan here who runs security and renee on infra, um we're evaluating redwood for an internal clinical notes summarization pipeline.
[00:20] Ethan Park: yeah hi, main thing for us is HIPAA scope and control over PHI, plus auditability, so i want to understand where keys live, who can see logs, like that.
[00:33] Priya Kapoor: great, thanks. quick note i'm priya, se at redwood. to set expectations we'll cover hosted, dedicated, and private deployment models and the security controls available in each. 
[00:45] Alex Chen: i can kick off with the compliance side — redwood has SOC2 type II and ISO27001 certs, we also provide pen test summaries and our latest attestation. i'll share the reports after the call.
[00:58] Ethan Park: okay SOC2's good, do you have any HIPAA-specific documentation or BAAs? that's critical for us.
[01:07] Alex Chen: yes we do offer a BAA for enterprise customers, typically paired with dedicated or private deployments. hosted customers can do business associate agreement under certain plans — i'll send specifics.
[01:20] Renee Liu: question on logging — how long are audit logs retained and can we export them to our SIEM? we want immutable logs for at least 1 year.
[01:30] Priya Kapoor: good question — by default hosted retention is 90 days, but for Dedicated and Private you can extend retention, and logs can be streamed to customer-managed sinks like S3/CloudWatch or Splunk. there is also support for immutable retention through our audit export pipeline.
[01:48] Sarah Martinez: can you clarify encryption at rest key ownership? we require customer-managed KMS for keys containing PHI.
[01:57] Priya Kapoor: for hosted we offer envelope encryption with keys managed by redwood; however for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS/HSM integrations — you can hold the root key. effectively you can control key rotation and revoke access.
[02:12] Ethan Park: and are model inputs/outputs logged by default? i'd rather not have full transcripts retained in logs.
[02:20] Priya Kapoor: by default we do not persist full-text request bodies in long-term logs for Hosted — we keep a short audit trail with metadata; payload retention is configurable. for Dedicated/Private we can disable storing request payloads entirely or redact at the service layer. there are tradeoffs for debugging and observability.
[02:41] Alex Chen: also want to call out RBAC — redwood supports role-based access controls with least privilege roles, SSO via SAML and OIDC, and SCIM for user provisioning. you can map your IdP groups to roles.
[02:56] Renee Liu: is there MFA enforced? and can we restrict API key creation to certain admins?
[03:03] Priya Kapoor: yes MFA enforced via IdP. API key creation and rotation policies can be restricted to admin roles; in Dedicated you get per-team namespaces and token scoping.
[03:15] Ethan Park: audit logs — are they tamper-evident? we need cryptographic integrity or an append-only store.
[03:22] Priya Kapoor: we can provide append-only export to your sink; for hosted we maintain internal integrity checks and provide signed export bundles on request. for the highest assurance we recommend Private deployment with customer-managed storage.
[03:38] Sarah Martinez: what about network controls — VPC peering, private endpoints? we want no internet egress for PHI.
[03:45] Priya Kapoor: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints; Private/on-prem gives you full network isolation — no public egress unless you configure it.
[03:56] Alex Chen: there was a question earlier about data residency — we can pin workloads to region and use region-specific storage to meet residency requirements.
[04:05] Renee Liu: latency concerns — if we go private on-prem we might get better data locality but do you have a recommended runtime footprint?
[04:12] Priya Kapoor: yes we'll share a deployment matrix; for clinical workloads we often recommend Dedicated in their cloud region with CMK to balance latency, cost, and compliance. Private on-prem is possible but requires infra effort.
[04:26] Ethan Park: ok on SSO/SAML integration — do you support inbound SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning? any large customers using Okta or Azure AD?
[04:35] Priya Kapoor: yes SAML 2.0 and OIDC both supported, SCIM v2 for provisioning. we have customers on Okta, Azure AD, and Ping. mapping groups to RBAC roles is standard.
[04:45] Sarah Martinez: another compliance question — do you provide audit-ready evidence for controls? like access logs, change control history, config snapshots?
[04:53] Alex Chen: yes we have an audit pack for enterprise deals that includes logs, change history, and config snapshots, plus attestation docs. i'll attach sample artifacts.
[05:03] Renee Liu: any encryption in transit specifics? TLS versions, mutual TLS?
[05:08] Priya Kapoor: TLS 1.2+ enforced, we can offer mTLS for private endpoints if needed.
[05:15] Ethan Park: how do you handle model updates and validation? we need to ensure model changes are traceable and prior versions can be pinned for audits.
[05:25] Priya Kapoor: version pinning is supported, rollouts can be canary or A/B, and we maintain model provenance metadata. we also integrate eval suites so you can tie quality regressions to rollouts.
[05:40] Sarah Martinez: what about data retention policies — can we auto-delete raw inputs after processing?
[05:48] Priya Kapoor: yes retention rules can be configured per-route; you can set TTLs and redaction pipelines to remove PII. for PHI we recommend no raw storage and immediate redaction.
[06:00] Alex Chen: wrapping up, looks like next steps are: i'll send SOC2/ISO docs and BAA details; priya will prepare deployment and latency/cost matrix; ethan to share retention policy.
[06:12] Sarah Martinez: that works, can we aim to have the deep dive next week? renee is available tuesday.
[06:18] Alex Chen: sure i'll propose tuesday 10am PT, priya will join with infra notes.
[06:24] Priya Kapoor: i'll also run a short benchmark with sample payloads to show token latency.
[06:30] Ethan Park: perfect, thanks everyone.
